title: OpenAI's latest AI models are coming to Google Cloud and Antigravity
gist: Google and OpenAI struck a deal to bring OpenAI's GPT 6 and 6.1 models (Astra, Sol, Luna) to Google Cloud's Model Garden and the Antigravity coding tool, starting in private preview; Google says it is now the only large cloud offering all three leading closed LLMs.

insights.claim: OpenAI's frontier GPT models will arrive in Google Cloud's Model Garden within weeks, and the full GPT 6 and 6.1 suite (Astra, Sol, Luna) will launch there, with Astra the most expensive to run.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Frontier-model distribution is going multi-cloud, weakening exclusivity as a moat for any single cloud.
insights.locator: For enterprise customers and AI enthusiasts

insights.claim: OpenAI says Microsoft remains its primary cloud partner even as its models run entirely on Google's infrastructure and bill through the Google Cloud Marketplace.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Microsoft's hold on OpenAI inference is loosening; watch Azure's share of OpenAI workloads.
insights.locator: While OpenAI notes that Microsoft continues

insights.claim: Google says it is now the only large cloud provider offering all three leading closed LLMs (Gemini, GPT and Claude), alongside 200-plus models in Model Garden.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Neutral model marketplace positioning is Google Cloud's competitive pitch versus rivals.
insights.locator: Google says it’s now the only large cloud provider

insights.claim: Billing through the Google Cloud Marketplace lets firms with existing Google Cloud spending commitments adopt GPT models in place of their current models without new procurement.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Commitment drawdown lowers friction for enterprises, shifting spend toward OpenAI via Google.
insights.locator: OpenAI models will be available to run entirely

insights.claim: GPT models will also appear in Google's Antigravity agentic coding client, which until now supported Gemini and Claude, though Google has not said which GPT models.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Coding-agent tools are becoming model-agnostic, shifting competition to model quality and price.

insights.claim: Google's new Gemini 4 Argon brings its flagship back to parity with competitors by Google's account and improves on Gemini 3.1 Pro, but burns through tokens at an astonishing rate, giving customers a reason to want alternatives.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: High token consumption raises customer cost, increasing demand for alternative models on Google Cloud.
insights.locator: Google recently rolled out Gemini 4 Argon
